items.question: What is the total length of the H125 (AS350 B3 2B1) helicopter?
items.explanation: The helicopter's total length is 12.94 meters (42.45 ft).

items.question: What is the diameter of the main rotor on the H125?
items.explanation: The main rotor diameter is 10.69 meters (35.07 ft).

items.question: Which engine powers the H125 (AS350 B3 2B1)?
items.explanation: The helicopter is powered by a Turbomeca Arriel 2B1 engine.

items.question: What is the maximum takeoff power rating (MTOP) of the Arriel 2B1 engine?
items.explanation: The Arriel 2B1 engine has a maximum takeoff power rating (MTOP) of 557 kW (747 SHP).

items.question: What is the nominal rotor speed of the main rotor?
items.explanation: The main rotor speed is 386 rpm.

items.question: What is the nominal tail rotor speed?
items.explanation: The nominal tail rotor speed is 2044 rpm.

items.question: What do red warning lights on the caution and warning panel (CWP) indicate?
options: Alarms requiring action which can be delayed
items.explanation: Red warning lights signal alarms requiring immediate action by the pilot.

items.question: How are audio alarms generated in the H125?
items.explanation: Audio alarms are generated through the intercommunication system when the HORN switch is ON.

items.question: The Turbomeca Arriel 2B1 engine in the H125 is classified as what type?
items.explanation: The Arriel 2B1 is a 650 kW class turboshaft engine designed for helicopters.

items.question: How many independent modules make up the Arriel 2B1 engine?
items.explanation: The engine is composed of five modules: Axial Compressor, Gas Generator, Free Turbine, Reduction Gear, and Output Shaft.

items.question: Which module reduces the free turbine speed from 39,158 rpm down to 6,000 rpm?
items.explanation: The Reduction Gear Module reduces turbine speed from 39,158 rpm to 6,000 rpm for transmission use.

items.question: What does the Output Shaft Module transmit power to?
options: The main rotor and accessory drive couplings
items.explanation: The Output Shaft Module transmits power to the MGB and accessory drive couplings.

items.question: What are the two subsystems of the engine oil system?
items.explanation: The engine oil system is divided into an external and an internal system.

items.question: What components are included in the external oil system?
items.explanation: The external system includes one tank and one cooler, with fireproof hoses.

items.question: How many scavenge pumps are part of the internal oil system?
items.explanation: The internal oil system includes one pressure pump and three scavenge pumps.

items.question: What is the purpose of the tank booster pump in the H125 fuel system?
options: To prime the fuel line during starting
items.explanation: The booster pump primes the fuel line during starting to ensure proper fuel delivery.

items.question: What does the hydro-mechanical unit of the FADEC control?
items.explanation: The hydro-mechanical unit of the FADEC is responsible for controlling engine fuel flow.

items.question: At what minimum temperature does the fuel heat exchanger allow operation without anti-ice additive?
items.explanation: The fuel system heat exchanger enables operation down to –20°C without requiring anti-ice additive.

items.question: How many Ancillary System Unit (ASU) cards manage the ancillary service functions of the helicopter?
items.explanation: Three ASU cards manage all audio warnings, some visual warnings, processing of specific electrical signals, and the engine fuel control back-up system.

items.question: Which ASU card is part of the Engine Back-up Control Ancillary Unit (EBCAU)?
items.explanation: ASU No.3 is part of the EBCAU and handles engine Nf signal acquisition and computing/signal processing for the back-up fuel metering valve.

items.question: What three operating modes does the VEMD provide?
items.explanation: The VEMD has three operating modes: OPERATIONAL (main mode, ground and flight), CONFIGURATION (ground only), and MAINTENANCE (ground only).

items.question: Which pages are available in the VEMD's OPERATIONAL mode?
options: ENGINE, VEHICLE, FLI, FLIGHT REPORT, and ENGINE POWER CHECK
items.explanation: OPERATIONAL mode contains the ENGINE, VEHICLE, FLI, FLIGHT REPORT and ENGINE POWER CHECK pages.

items.question: What happens automatically if a parameter on the VEMD's FLI (First Limitation Indicator) page becomes invalid?
options: The ENGINE page is automatically displayed so the parameters can be read on independent scales
The aircraft reverts to CONFIGURATION mode
Nothing; the FLI page remains frozen
items.explanation: If a FLI page parameter becomes invalid, the ENGINE page is automatically displayed so the parameters can be read on independent scales.

items.question: On the VEMD PERFORMANCE page, what is the default crew weight (CREW) used at power-up?
items.explanation: At power-up, the default CREW weight value on the PERFORMANCE page is 80 kg (176 lb).

items.question: When does the VEMD's FLIGHT REPORT page automatically replace the VEHICLE page?
options: When the aircraft lands on a helipad
When the VEMD detects engine shutdown and NR below 70 rpm
When the fuel level drops below 10%
items.explanation: The FLIGHT REPORT page automatically replaces the VEHICLE page once the VEMD detects engine shutdown with NR below 70 rpm.

items.question: Where is the hydraulic pressure cut-off switch located?
items.explanation: The hydraulic pressure cut-off switch is mounted on the collective lever grip.

items.question: What other flight controls, besides the collective and cyclic grips, are described in Section 7.5?
options: Rotor brake and fuel shut-off control, and the EBCAU test switch / engine starting selector
Autopilot disconnect and altitude hold switches
items.explanation: Section 7.5 also covers the rotor brake and fuel shut-off control (with their safety devices) and the guarded EBCAU test switch with the engine starting selector.

items.question: The forward adjustable spot light used for emergency cabin lighting is supplied directly by which source?
items.explanation: The forward spot light is supplied directly by the battery for use as an emergency light in case of total lighting failure.

items.question: What does exterior lighting on the H125 comprise?
options: Three position lights, an anti-collision light, a fixed taxi light, and a fixed or swiveling landing light
Two position lights and a searchlight only
A rotating beacon and two landing lights
items.explanation: Exterior lighting includes three position lights, an anti-collision light, a fixed taxi light, and a fixed or swiveling landing light.

items.question: What does the MGB (main gearbox) drive and support, besides transmitting power to the main rotor?
options: The hydraulic pump, the MGB lubricating pump, and the rotor brake
Only the tail rotor drive shaft
items.explanation: The MGB transmits engine power to the main rotor with speed reduction, and drives/supports the hydraulic pump, the MGB lubricating pump, and the rotor brake.

items.question: How is the tail gearbox (TGB) lubricated?
options: By a dedicated electric oil pump
It shares the MGB's pressurized oil system
items.explanation: The TGB is splash-lubricated and includes a visual oil level indicator and a chip detection caution light.

items.question: What type of main rotor hub does the H125 use, and what is distinctive about it?
options: STARFLEX hub, with no ball bearings and no lubrication system
A fully articulated hub with elastomeric bearings requiring regular lubrication
A teetering hub identical to the tail rotor
A rigid hub with hydraulic dampers
items.explanation: The semi-rigid "STARFLEX" main rotor hub has no ball bearings nor a lubrication system; flapping is achieved through the composite star arms, with lead-lag and pitch hinges via elastomeric items.

items.question: How many main rotor servos does the hydraulic system power, and how are they arranged?
options: Three: one longitudinal and two lateral
Two: one longitudinal and one lateral
Four: two longitudinal and two lateral
One combined servo for all axes
items.explanation: There are three main rotor servos (one longitudinal, two lateral) plus a separate tail rotor servo for yaw control.

items.question: What is the hydraulic system's pressure regulating valve set to?
items.explanation: The regulator unit's pressure regulating valve is set to 40 bar (580 psi).

items.question: After a hydraulic pressure loss, what is the recommended safety speed range the pilot should reach?
items.explanation: The recommended safety speed range is 40 to 60 kt (74 to 111 km/h); the average time to reach it from VNE or hover is less than 30 seconds.

items.question: What distinguishes SAMM main rotor servos from Dunlop servos?
options: SAMM servos have an input clearance locking system; Dunlop servos do not
Dunlop servos are electrically actuated; SAMM servos are not
SAMM servos only work on the tail rotor
There is no functional difference between them
items.explanation: SAMM servos include an input clearance locking system to reduce control freeplay in bypass mode, which can cause a brief cyclic movement during pressurization; Dunlop lateral servos do not have this device.

items.question: What two hydraulic tests should be performed before each flight as a normal procedure?
options: The hydraulic accumulator test and the hydraulic pressure cut-off test
The fuel dump test and the generator test
The rotor brake test and the FADEC reset test
The battery load test and the AC inverter test
items.explanation: Before each flight: the accumulator test (ACCU TST/HYD TEST) checks accumulator assistance, and the hydraulic cut-off test checks the main servo dump electro-valves.

items.question: Which three sources supply the DC electrical network?
options: A starter generator, a 15 A/h battery, and a 28 V external power unit (EPU) receptacle
Two batteries and a wind-driven generator
A fuel cell, a battery, and a solar panel
Only the starter generator and the EPU
items.explanation: The DC network is supplied by a starter generator on the engine accessory gearbox, a 15 A/h battery, and an EPU receptacle (400 A max).

items.question: What is the current rating of the generator (standard/optional)?
items.explanation: The generator is rated at 150 A, with 200 A as an optional rating.

items.question: What does the amber INV caution light on the CWP indicate?
options: The inverter is not operating, or the AC power generating system has failed
items.explanation: The amber INV caution light indicates the inverter is not operating, or there is a failure of the AC power generating system.

items.question: What does the amber PITOT caution light indicate?
options: The pitot heating system is not operating, is OFF, or has failed
The static ports are blocked by ice
The VEMD has lost airspeed data entirely
items.explanation: The amber PITOT caution light indicates the pitot tube heating system is not operating, is switched OFF, or has failed.

items.question: How is cabin heating and demisting air produced?
options: By mixing hot P2 air bled from the engine with outside air drawn from under the cabin floor
By an electric resistive heater in the cabin floor
By diverting exhaust gas directly into the cabin
items.explanation: Heating and demisting are achieved by mixing hot P2 air bled from the engine with outside air drawn from under the cabin floor, channelled to heating and demisting outlets.

items.question: On the APPAREO Vision 1000 status LED, what does a steady green light mean?
items.explanation: Green indicates normal operation. Red indicates a fault, blue indicates the boot sequence, and yellow indicates an SD card, formatting, or GPS issue.
